review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

1:1.sourceText: Παῦλος δοῦλος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, κλητὸς ἀπόστολος ἀφωρισμένος εἰς εὐαγγέλιον Θεοῦ,
1:1.targetText: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—

groups.note: κλητός ("called") is an adjective: "a called apostle".

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an infinitive copula after called.
English joins the participle ἀφωρισμένος ("set apart") with and; the Greek has no καί here.

1:2.sourceText: ὃ προεπηγγείλατο διὰ τῶν προφητῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν γραφαῖς ἁγίαις
1:2.targetText: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,

groups.note: The relative ὅ ("which") is rendered by its antecedent, the gospel.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:3.sourceText: περὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ τοῦ γενομένου ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυεὶδ κατὰ σάρκα,
1:3.targetText: regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,

groups.note: The article with γενομένου ("having come") is rendered who was.
ἐκ σπέρματος ("from the seed") is rendered a descendant.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:4.sourceText: τοῦ ὁρισθέντος Υἱοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν δυνάμει κατὰ πνεῦμα ἁγιωσύνης ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν,
1:4.targetText: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.

groups.note: The article with the participle ὁρισθέντος ("declared") is rendered who was declared.
κατά ("according to") is rendered through.
ἐξ ("from, out of") is rendered by.
The genitive νεκρῶν ("of the dead") is rendered from the dead.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the second article-participle clause with and; the Greek has no καί here.
English supplies an infinitive copula after declared.
English supplies the possessive; the Greek has no pronoun here.

1:5.sourceText: δι’ οὗ ἐλάβομεν χάριν καὶ ἀποστολὴν εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ,
1:5.targetText: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.

groups.note: The relative οὗ ("whom") is rendered Him.
εἰς ("into, for") is rendered to before the obedience.
The genitive πίστεως ("of faith") is rendered from faith.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb for the purpose phrase; the Greek has no word for call.
English supplies a pronoun so that all stands as a noun.
English joins the moved phrase on behalf of His name with and; the Greek has no καί here.
English supplies a relative frame for the genitive.

1:6.sourceText: ἐν οἷς ἐστε καὶ ὑμεῖς κλητοὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
1:6.targetText: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.

groups.note: The relative οἷς ("whom") is rendered those who.
The genitive Ἰησοῦ ("of Jesus") is rendered to belong to Jesus.

unmappedTarget.reason: English begins a new sentence with And; the Greek continues with a relative clause.
English supplies a copula.

1:7.sourceText: πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Ῥώμῃ ἀγαπητοῖς Θεοῦ, κλητοῖς ἁγίοις· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:7.targetText: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints:  Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

groups.note: τοῖς οὖσιν ("who are") is placed after in Rome.
The genitive Θεοῦ ("of God") is rendered by God.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the two descriptions with and; the Greek has no καί here.
English supplies an infinitive copula after called.

1:8.sourceText: Πρῶτον μὲν εὐχαριστῶ τῷ Θεῷ μου διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καταγγέλλεται ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ.
1:8.targetText: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.

groups.note: ἐν ("in") is rendered over; with ὅλῳ it gives all over.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the particle μέν untranslated; no δέ answers it.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:9.sourceText: μάρτυς γάρ μού ἐστιν ὁ Θεός, ᾧ λατρεύω ἐν τῷ πνεύματί μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἀδιαλείπτως μνείαν ὑμῶν ποιοῦμαι
1:9.targetText: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you

groups.note: μνείαν ποιοῦμαι ("I make mention") is rendered I remember.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the activity; the Greek says only "in the gospel".

1:10.sourceText: πάντοτε ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου, δεόμενος εἴ πως ἤδη ποτὲ εὐοδωθήσομαι ἐν τῷ θελήματι τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
1:10.targetText: in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.

groups.note: εἴ πως ("if somehow") is rendered that.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:11.sourceText: ἐπιποθῶ γὰρ ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἵνα τι μεταδῶ χάρισμα ὑμῖν πνευματικὸν εἰς τὸ στηριχθῆναι ὑμᾶς,
1:11.targetText: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,

groups.note: εἰς τό with the infinitive marks purpose, rendered to.
The passive στηριχθῆναι ("to be strengthened") is rendered strengthen.

1:12.sourceText: τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν συνπαρακληθῆναι ἐν ὑμῖν διὰ τῆς ἐν ἀλλήλοις πίστεως ὑμῶν τε καὶ ἐμοῦ.
1:12.targetText: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.

groups.note: ἐν ἀλλήλοις ("in one another") is rendered each other's.
BSB makes ὑμῶν ("yours") the subject you.
BSB makes ἐμοῦ ("mine") the subject I.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB folds ἐν ὑμῖν ("among you") into the subject you and I.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders τε … καί as a plain and, so τε has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the infinitive with that.

1:13.sourceText: οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι πολλάκις προεθέμην ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἐκωλύθην ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, ἵνα τινὰ καρπὸν σχῶ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς καὶ ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν.
1:13.targetText: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.

groups.note: ὅτι ("that") is rendered how.
καί ("and") is rendered but.
τοῦ δεῦρο ("the present") is rendered now.
τινά ("some") is rendered a.
καρπόν ("fruit") is rendered harvest.
The verb σχῶ is understood again in the comparison and BSB repeats it.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies what was prevented.
English adds a perfect tense to the repeated verb; the Greek states no verb here.

1:14.sourceText: Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ Βαρβάροις, σοφοῖς τε καὶ ἀνοήτοις ὀφειλέτης εἰμί·
1:14.targetText: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.

groups.note: ὀφειλέτης ("debtor") is rendered obligated.

1:15.sourceText: οὕτως τὸ κατ’ ἐμὲ πρόθυμον καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐν Ῥώμῃ εὐαγγελίσασθαι.
1:15.targetText: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.

groups.note: οὕτως ("so, thus") is rendered That is why.
κατ’ ἐμέ ("as for me") is rendered I.

unmappedSource.reason: The article τό, which makes πρόθυμον a noun ("eagerness"), has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula.
English adds an intensifying adverb.
English supplies a copula.

1:16.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ἐπαισχύνομαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον· δύναμις γὰρ Θεοῦ ἐστιν εἰς σωτηρίαν παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι.
1:16.targetText: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.

groups.note: γάρ ("for") is rendered because.
καί ("and") is rendered then after first.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
BSB renders τε … καί as first … then, so τε has no separate English word.

1:17.sourceText: δικαιοσύνη γὰρ Θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν, καθὼς γέγραπται Ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται.
1:17.targetText: For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτῷ ("it") is rendered the gospel.
The passive ἀποκαλύπτεται ("is revealed") is rendered reveals.

targetPhrases.text: by faith from start to finish

groups.note: ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν ("from faith to faith") is rendered by faith from start to finish.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes the gospel the subject, so ἐν ("in") has no English word.
BSB leaves the connective δέ in the quotation untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative frame before by faith.

1:18.sourceText: Ἀποκαλύπτεται γὰρ ὀργὴ Θεοῦ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ἀσέβειαν καὶ ἀδικίαν ἀνθρώπων τῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐν ἀδικίᾳ κατεχόντων,
1:18.targetText: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive; the Greek has no pronoun here.

1:19.sourceText: διότι τὸ γνωστὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ φανερόν ἐστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς· ὁ Θεὸς γὰρ αὐτοῖς ἐφανέρωσεν.
1:19.targetText: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.

groups.note: διότι ("because") is rendered For.
γνωστόν ("known, knowable") is rendered may be known.
ἐν ("in, among") is rendered to.
γάρ ("for") is rendered because.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of has made plain.

1:20.sourceText: τὰ γὰρ ἀόρατα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου τοῖς ποιήμασιν νοούμενα καθορᾶται, ἥ τε ἀΐδιος αὐτοῦ δύναμις καὶ θειότης, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἀναπολογήτους,
1:20.targetText: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered God's.
ἀπό ("from") is rendered since.
The article τοῖς is rendered as the possessive His.
εἰς τό with the infinitive is rendered so that.
The pronoun αὐτούς ("them") is rendered men.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders τε … καί as a plain and, so τε has no separate English word.

1:21.sourceText: διότι γνόντες τὸν Θεὸν οὐχ ὡς Θεὸν ἐδόξασαν ἢ ηὐχαρίστησαν, ἀλλὰ ἐματαιώθησαν ἐν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία.
1:21.targetText: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.

groups.note: ἤ ("or") is rendered nor after neither.
BSB makes the subject καρδία ("heart") a phrase: in their foolish hearts.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle γνόντες ("knowing").
English supplies the object of glorified.
English supplies the object of gave thanks.

1:22.targetText: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle φάσκοντες ("claiming").

1:23.sourceText: καὶ ἤλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ ἀφθάρτου Θεοῦ ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος φθαρτοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πετεινῶν καὶ τετραπόδων καὶ ἑρπετῶν.
1:23.targetText: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.

groups.note: ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος ("the likeness of an image") is rendered images.

1:24.sourceText: Διὸ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῶν καρδιῶν αὐτῶν εἰς ἀκαθαρσίαν τοῦ ἀτιμάζεσθαι τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς,
1:24.targetText: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.

groups.note: The genitive article with the infinitive ἀτιμάζεσθαι ("to be dishonored") is rendered for the dishonoring.
αὐτοῖς ("themselves") is rendered one another.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:25.sourceText: οἵτινες μετήλλαξαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ψεύδει, καὶ ἐσεβάσθησαν καὶ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν Κτίσαντα, ὅς ἐστιν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
1:25.targetText: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.

groups.note: The relative οἵτινες ("who") begins a new English sentence as They.
εὐλογητός ("blessed") is rendered worthy of praise.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:26.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Θεὸς εἰς πάθη ἀτιμίας· αἵ τε γὰρ θήλειαι αὐτῶν μετήλλαξαν τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν εἰς τὴν παρὰ φύσιν,
1:26.targetText: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

groups.note: The genitive ἀτιμίας ("of dishonor") is rendered dishonorable.
χρῆσιν ("use, function") is rendered relations.
The article τήν stands for χρῆσιν ("use") and is rendered ones.
παρὰ φύσιν ("against nature") is rendered unnatural.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render τε, which pairs with the τε καί of the next verse.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds an emphatic adverb.

1:27.sourceText: ὁμοίως τε καὶ οἱ ἄρσενες ἀφέντες τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν τῆς θηλείας ἐξεκαύθησαν ἐν τῇ ὀρέξει αὐτῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους, ἄρσενες ἐν ἄρσεσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην κατεργαζόμενοι καὶ τὴν ἀντιμισθίαν ἣν ἔδει τῆς πλάνης αὐτῶν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀπολαμβάνοντες.
1:27.targetText: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.

groups.note: ἣν ἔδει ("which was necessary") is rendered due.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders ὁμοίως τε καί as Likewise, so τε has no separate English word.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated after Likewise.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτῶν ("their") untranslated with lust.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀφέντες ("having abandoned") to burned with and; the Greek has no καί here.
English adds other for clarity.

1:28.sourceText: Καὶ καθὼς οὐκ ἐδοκίμασαν τὸν Θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἐπιγνώσει, παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Θεὸς εἰς ἀδόκιμον νοῦν, ποιεῖν τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα,
1:28.targetText: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.

groups.note: καί ("and") is rendered Furthermore.
ἔχειν ἐν ἐπιγνώσει ("to have in knowledge") is rendered to acknowledge.
BSB renders Θεός ("God") as He.
The article with καθήκοντα ("fitting things") is rendered what ought to be done.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:29.sourceText: πεπληρωμένους πάσῃ ἀδικίᾳ πονηρίᾳ πλεονεξίᾳ κακίᾳ, μεστοὺς φθόνου φόνου ἔριδος δόλου κακοηθείας, ψιθυριστάς,
1:29.targetText: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle πεπληρωμένους ("filled").
English adds and before the last item; the Greek list has no καί.
English supplies a subject and copula.
English adds and before the last item; the Greek list has no καί.
English supplies a subject and copula.

1:30.sourceText: καταλάλους, θεοστυγεῖς, ὑβριστάς, ὑπερηφάνους, ἀλαζόνας, ἐφευρετὰς κακῶν, γονεῦσιν ἀπειθεῖς,
1:30.targetText: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.

groups.note: The noun ἐφευρετάς ("inventors") is rendered invent.
The plural κακῶν ("evil things") is rendered forms of evil.
The adjective ἀπειθεῖς ("disobedient") is rendered disobey.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds and before the last item; the Greek list has no καί.
English supplies a subject.
English adds new to bring out the idea of inventing.
English supplies the possessive.
English supplies a subject.

1:31.targetText: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula.

1:32.sourceText: οἵτινες τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπιγνόντες, ὅτι οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντες ἄξιοι θανάτου εἰσίν, οὐ μόνον αὐτὰ ποιοῦσιν, ἀλλὰ καὶ συνευδοκοῦσιν τοῖς πράσσουσιν.
1:32.targetText: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.

groups.note: The relative οἵτινες ("who") is rendered they.
αὐτά ("them") is rendered these things.
The present ποιοῦσιν ("they do") is rendered continue to do.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The article τά has no separate English word in such things.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of practice.
